Title: Log Transaction Creation
I want: to automatically log each transaction creation (insert) with transaction ID, name, user ID, timestamp, and channel
So that: there is a complete audit trail of when and by whom each transaction was created
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System logs an entry whenever a new transaction record is inserted in any tracked business table (Purchase Order, Sales Invoice, etc.).
2. Log entry includes: Transaction ID, Transaction Name, Action Type = 'Insert', User ID, Timestamp, Channel (Web/Mobile App).
3. Logging does not delay the transaction commit (asynchronous).
4. Log entries are stored in a separate transaction_logs table.
5. User ID is captured from the authenticated session.
Preconditions: User is logged in and performs a transaction insert operation via Web or Mobile App.
Postconditions: A record is created in transaction_logs table with all required fields.
Action Buttons: View Transaction Logs, Filter by Date, Export

Title: Log Transaction Update
I want: to capture each transaction update action including which user modified the transaction and when
So that: changes to critical transactions are traceable and accountable
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System logs an entry whenever an existing transaction record is updated.
2. Log entry includes: Transaction ID, Transaction Name, Action Type = 'Update', User ID, Timestamp, Channel.
3. Only the fact of update is logged, not field-level changes (per BRD out of scope).
4. Multiple updates to same transaction create multiple log entries.
5. Asynchronous logging ensures no performance impact.
Preconditions: Transaction record exists, user performs update operation.
Postconditions: New record in transaction_logs with Action Type 'Update'.
Action Buttons: View Transaction History, Filter by Transaction ID, Export Audit Trail

Title: Log Approval Workflow Decisions
I want: to log each approval decision (Approve/Reject/Sent Back) with workflow stage, transaction ID, user, and timestamp
So that: the approval history of any transaction can be reviewed for compliance
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System logs an entry whenever an approval action is taken in a workflow.
2. Log entry includes: Transaction ID, Transaction Name, Workflow Name, Stage, Action (Approve/Reject/Send Back), User ID, Timestamp.
3. Each decision is logged individually, including sequential approvals.
4. Logs are stored in workflow_approval_logs table.
5. Decision-level only, no step-by-step system logs (per BRD).
Preconditions: Workflow engine is available, transaction is under approval process.
Action Buttons: View Approval History, Filter by Transaction, Filter by Approver

Title: Log Workflow Configuration Changes
I want: to log high-level workflow configuration changes (create/update) with user and timestamp
So that: any unauthorized or incorrect workflow changes can be traced back
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System logs an entry whenever a workflow is created or its configuration is updated.
2. Log entry includes: Workflow Name, Action (Create/Update), User ID, Timestamp.
3. Only configuration changes are logged, not runtime workflow instances.
4. Logs are stored in workflow_config_logs table.
5. Asynchronous logging applies.
Preconditions: Workflow configuration feature exists, user with admin rights modifies workflow.
Action Buttons: View Config Change Log, Filter by Workflow Name, Export

Title: Log Report Execution and Duration
I want: to capture each report execution with report name, user, start time, end time, and calculated duration
So that: I can analyze which reports are used most frequently and identify performance bottlenecks
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System logs an entry whenever a user executes a report.
2. Log entry includes: Report Name, User ID, Start Time, End Time, Duration (system calculated in seconds/milliseconds).
3. Logging is asynchronous and does not delay report rendering.
4. Logs are stored in report_logs table.
5. Duration is automatically calculated as End Time - Start Time.
Preconditions: Report is available, user has permission to run report.
Postconditions: Report log entry created after report execution completes.
Action Buttons: View Report Usage Analytics, Filter by Date Range, Export Performance Data

Title: Implement Asynchronous Logging Framework
I want: all logging operations to be processed asynchronously (background queue) without blocking the main transaction thread
So that: system performance remains optimal even under high log volume
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Logging API returns immediately without waiting for write to disk/database.
2. Log entries are queued and written in background process with configurable batch size.
3. Acceptable delay for log visibility is up to a few minutes (per BRD).
4. If queue is full, logs are dropped with warning (no impact on main transaction).
5. Separate database connection pool for logging to avoid contention.
Preconditions: System is running with logging enabled.
Postconditions: Logs eventually appear in respective tables without noticeable performance degradation.
Action Buttons: View Queue Status, Configure Batch Settings, Monitor Logging Health

Title: Create Separate Log Tables with Optimized Indexing
I want: logs to be stored in separate tables (transaction_logs, workflow_approval_logs, workflow_config_logs, report_logs) with appropriate indexes for querying
So that: reporting on logs does not impact production transaction tables and queries run efficiently
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Log tables are in a separate schema or database from transactional tables.
2. Each log table has indexes on: Timestamp (for date range queries), User ID, Transaction ID (for transaction logs), Report Name (for report logs).
3. No foreign keys to transactional tables to avoid locking.
4. Partitioning by date (monthly) is implemented for archiving.
5. Indexes are reviewed quarterly for performance.
Postconditions: Log tables created with indexes, insert performance meets SLA (under 10ms for queued writes).
Action Buttons: Rebuild Indexes, Show Table Sizes, Archive Old Logs

Title: Implement Log Archival and Retention
I want: to automatically archive log data older than 3-6 months to a compressed storage and purge from live system
So that: storage costs are controlled and live log query performance remains fast
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Scheduled job runs daily to identify logs older than retention period (configurable, default 6 months).
2. Old logs are exported to compressed CSV/Parquet files and stored in designated archive location.
3. After successful archival, purged from live log tables.
4. Archived logs can be re-imported for compliance audit if needed.
5. Retention period can be adjusted (3 months, 6 months, 12 months) via configuration.
6. Archived logs are encrypted at rest.
Preconditions: Archive storage location configured, scheduled job setup.
Postconditions: Live log tables contain only recent logs within retention period, archive files created.
Action Buttons: Trigger Archive Now, Restore from Archive, Set Retention Policy, View Archive Status

Title: View Unified Audit Trail Dashboard
I want: a dashboard that shows combined audit logs from transactions, workflows, and reports with filtering by date, user, and action type
So that: I can perform comprehensive compliance audits without querying multiple tables manually
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Dashboard page with tabs: All Logs, Transaction Logs, Workflow Logs, Report Logs.
2. Columns: Timestamp, User ID, Action Type (Insert/Update/Approve/Reject/etc.), Entity Type (Transaction/Workflow/Report), Entity ID (Transaction ID/Workflow Name/Report Name), Channel.
3. Filters: Date Range, User, Action Type, Entity Type.
4. Search by keyword across log details.
5. Export filtered results to CSV/Excel.
6. Pagination and sorting by timestamp descending.
Postconditions: User can view and export logs.
Action Buttons: Apply Filters, Export CSV, Reset Filters, View Details

Title: Validate Performance Impact of Logging
I want: to run load tests that measure transaction response time with and without logging enabled, ensuring degradation is under 5%
So that: business teams are confident that logging does not slow down operations
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Load test: 1000 concurrent transactions per minute, measure average response time.
2. With logging enabled, average response time increase is less than 5% compared to no logging.
3. Asynchronous queue never exceeds 1000 pending logs under peak load.
4. No transaction failures due to logging queue overflow.
5. CPU and memory usage increase for logging process stays within 10% of total.
Postconditions: Performance report generated, meets success criteria.
Action Buttons: Run Performance Test, View Metrics, Export Report
